systems.system: Central African Backbone (CAB), CAR-Congo interconnection via Bomassa
systems.country_label: Dorsale a fibre optique d'Afrique centrale

note: Document is about the CAR backbone; the Congo link is a cross-border interconnection and no statement is made about Congo's own national backbone.
Planned pan-African terrestrial fibre project listing Republic of Congo among its countries; a plan with no contract or works stated for COG.

facts.fact: Xalam Analytics says the Projet de Couverture Nationale fibre project is underway, about 3,000 km of terrestrial fibre connecting key towns; document gives no event date, so its published date (January 2026) is used.

Xalam Analytics describes the Central African Backbone (CAB) project as ongoing, expanding Congo's fibre backbone reach to secondary towns and neighbouring countries; no event date given, so the published date (January 2026) is used.

note: Passage says funding will pay for 600 km of cross-border fibre to be laid; money promised, no contract or works stated, and cross-border routes.
Congo Telecom talks on wholesale capacity with DRC operators; no statement about a national fibre backbone, its reach or terms.

systems.system: Projet de couverture nationale en infrastructures de télécommunications (PCN)
systems.owner: State; assets of phases 1-2 made available to Congo Telecom in usufruct, to be transferred to it by decree

note: Council of Ministers 2026-05-06 transfers PCN phase 1-3 assets (FCFA 143.9bn) to Congo Telecom, phase 3 under way, but never says fibre, backbone or regions connected, so no backbone fact.

systems.system: Urban aerial fibre networks of Congo Telecom, GVA (CanalBox), Silicon Connect

note: Urban fibre cabling and infrastructure sharing (metro); EEC power-network infrastructure use by telecom operators mentioned as a coming ARPCE agreement, no backbone fact.
Document states nothing this study asks.

facts.fact: The Treasury sheet says the PCN deployed about 3,000 km of fibre linking Pointe-Noire, Dolisie, Brazzaville, Oyo and Ouesso, operated and marketed by Congo Telecom, plus a 1,100 km secondary E2C network.

note: The Matombi-Pointe-Noire-Brazzaville backbone is only said to be financed; no contract or works stated.

facts.fact: Ecofin reports Congo launched construction of a second national fibre backbone in September 2023, to link Pointe-Noire and Brazzaville, with no recent progress update.
Xalam Analytics says the Projet de Couverture Nationale fibre project is underway, about 3,000km of terrestrial fibre connecting key towns, alongside the ongoing Central African Backbone project.

AfriqueITNews reports the Congolese government entrusted Silicone Connect under a public-private partnership with upgrading the national fibre network between Pointe-Noire and Brazzaville to 200 Gb, a EUR 3.2 million project launched on 12 July 2024.
AfriqueITNews reports the first phase, the southern backbone, was completed, moving from SDH to DWDM on the existing Pointe-Noire to Brazzaville fibre network.

systems.owner: Government of Congo, PPP with Silicone Connect
